log.reasoning: No history with any opponent yet, so I open by cooperating everywhere to build mutual cooperation. I will respond to defection in later rounds based on what each opponent actually does.
Round 1 with no information; open with cooperation to establish mutual cooperation in a long, noisy game.
Round 1 with no information: open by cooperating with everyone to establish mutual cooperation, then reciprocate while forgiving occasional defections that may be noise.
Round 1, no information. Since I only win by outscoring each opponent, defecting can never leave me behind in a round, so I open with D against everyone.
Round 1 with no information; opening with cooperation to establish mutual benefit, accepting noise risk.

Mirror each opponent's round-1 move: defect against A and D, who defected on me and have low reputations, and keep cooperating with C, E, F, G and H, who cooperated or were forgiving. Cooperation with the cooperative group keeps the 3-point payoffs flowing.
Tit-for-tat style: reciprocate cooperation, retaliate against round-1 defectors.
Generous tit-for-tat: cooperate with cooperators, forgive likely-noise defections from high-reputation players, defect against players who defected and have low reputation.
Defection never loses a match on relative score, so I defect against everyone.
Reciprocate cooperation; retaliate against defectors with poor reputation, forgive likely noise from those with good reputation.

A has never cooperated with me and has 0% reputation, so I defect against it. D is also a low-reputation defector and has defected on me after my cooperation, so I defect. The rest have cooperated with me or have high reputations, so I keep cooperating.
Defect on known defectors A and D, cooperate with the rest and forgive likely noise.

Defect against habitual defectors (A, D) and reciprocate E's defection given its mediocre reputation; forgive B's single defection as likely noise given its high reputation, and keep cooperating with cooperative C, G, H.
Goal is to outscore each opponent; D never loses ground relative to the opponent in a round, so defect everywhere.
Cooperate with reciprocators and forgive likely noise; defect against low-reputation or recently exploiting players.

A has 0% cooperation with others, so I defect against it. I keep cooperating with the reliable cooperators C, F, G and H, and I stay open with E, whose mixed record I read as noise rather than intent. I keep D at defection because it is almost never cooperative.
Defect on known defectors A and D; cooperate with the rest.
Cooperate with reliable cooperators and forgive likely noise; defect against low-reputation defectors.
Goal is to outscore each opponent head-to-head; defecting never scores less than the opponent in a round, so I defect against everyone.
Cooperate with reliable cooperators, defect against persistent defectors and low-reputation players.

A has defected every round and has a 0% reputation, so I defect against it. D has a very low reputation, so I defect there too. I cooperate with the high-reputation opponents who are cooperating, and with E, whose last move was C, to keep mutual cooperation going.
Defect on reputed defectors and alternating E, cooperate with steady cooperators.
Cooperate with cooperators and forgive likely noise; defect against near-pure defectors; probe E with cooperation since they cooperated last round.
Goal is to finish ahead in each match; D never loses relative points in any round, so defect against everyone.
Cooperate with partners who mostly cooperate; defect against persistent defectors.

A and D have shown almost no cooperation, so I defect against them. I cooperate with the reliably cooperative C, F and G, and with H, whose single defection in round 5 may be noise. E has defected in its most recent round, so I defect against it.
Cooperate with reciprocators, defect against consistent defectors.
Defect against persistent defectors (A, D) and the erratic E; keep cooperating with cooperative players, forgiving single defections as likely noise.
Relative score is what matters; D never loses a head-to-head and opponents mostly defect, so defect on all.
Defect against persistent defectors, cooperate with reciprocators.

A and D are near-permanent defectors, so I defect against them. C, F, G and H have cooperated with me consistently, and E cooperated after my recent defection, so I keep cooperating to hold mutual gains.
Cooperate with cooperators, defect on hostile or unresponsive players.
Cooperate with high-reputation cooperators and forgive isolated (likely noise-driven) defections; defect against persistent defectors and the erratic E.
Winning each match means finishing with more points than that opponent, and defecting never lowers my margin in a round, so I defect against everyone.
Defect against habitual defectors A and D; cooperate with the cooperative rest.
A and D almost never cooperate, so I defect against them. C, F, G and H mostly cooperate, so I keep cooperating to build mutual 3-point rounds. E is mixed, so I cooperate and watch for retaliation.

Defect on persistent defectors, cooperate with cooperators.
